_doc: Run-length method of the gem5 evaluation (read by sim/run_lengths.py, sim/run_experiments.py,
sim/baselines/oracle/oracle_sweep.py and sim/baselines/tune/tune_baselines.py). Bump 'version'
whenever a budget or the method changes: results record the version they were produced with.
Problem: the `large` inputs are 0.2-14 G RISC-V instructions; the O3 model runs at ~0.2 M inst/s
(6-20 h per run, x ~25 variants x 3 machines x 15 kernels). The `small` inputs (40-550 M) are
simulated in full.
Method for `large` (mode 'regions', region-aligned stratified sampling):
1. profile: one functional AtomicSimpleCPU pass of the kernel's `oracle` build (region(id)
markers only, docs/interfaces.md §5) records the instruction count at every region visit
(gem5 PcCountTracker probes on the marker PCs). Instructions before the first marker form
stratum -1. Output: results/runlen/<oracle variant dir>/<kernel>.<input>.json.
2. plan: per region, `per_region` visits (evenly spaced over its visits; 1 = the first) are
sampled. A sample starts `warmup_insts` before the visit's marker and measures
min(`measure_insts`, visit length) instructions, so the measurement starts at the region
boundary and stays inside the visit when the visit is shorter than the budget.
Regions whose total share is below `min_region_frac` are not sampled (their share is
reported as unsampled_frac). At most `max_samples` samples (largest strata first).
3. checkpoints: one functional pass per binary writes a gem5 checkpoint at every sample
start, plus the last setwin/region executed before it (se.py --take-checkpoints); it is
shared by every policy/machine that runs that binary (memory size is part of the key).
4. detailed: each sample restores its checkpoint into the O3 CPU, runs `warmup_insts`
detailed instructions (caches, predictors and the policies' period state warm up; stats
are reset at the end) and measures. Hint-driven policies start in the configuration of
the last setwin before the checkpoint (se.py --window-seed auto), so their state is
exact; the reactive policies learn during the warm-up.
5. merge: stats.txt = sum over samples of each sample's counters x (instructions of its
stratum / instructions it measured): a whole-program estimate (stratified estimator),
comparable across variants because every variant uses the same plan (same profile, same
starts, same budgets). stats.measured.txt is the unweighted sum. region_stats.csv keeps
the measured rows only (warm-up rows dropped), so the B1 oracle compares configurations
on exactly the same windows as the campaign.
Instruction offsets come from the `oracle` binary; plain/winhint/oracle_hinted/pgo/jones
binaries differ from it only by a handful of hint instructions outside hot loops, so the
same counts land at the same program points (well inside the warm-up). Clairvoyance (B8)
transforms the code: its samples cover the same instruction counts, not the same regions,
so compare B8 per instruction (IPC, energy/inst), not per region.
Modes: 'full' (whole program), 'regions' (above), 'fixed' (explicit 'starts' list; each
start gets warmup + measure; weights = 1, i.e. stats are the sum of the windows).
'full_below_insts': a profiled run whose total is below this is simulated in full.
Budget rationale: warmup 5 M instructions refills a 1-2 MB L2 (16-32 k lines) many times
for these streaming kernels and covers >= 5000 window periods of 1000 cycles; 20 M measured
instructions per visit cover several thousand periods of every policy (B4 intervals are
100 k instructions). With ~10-20 regions per kernel this is ~250-500 M detailed
instructions per run, i.e. the cost of a `small` run. Decoders sample 3 visits per region
(first, middle, last decode step) because attention work grows with the context.
